narrative:
The assessment estimated a 58.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning you were judged somewhat more likely than not to have repayment problems. Because this exceeds the bank’s cutoff, your application was denied.

The strongest reason was your checking account status. Your account is currently recorded as below zero DM, an overdrawn position seen among only about 12.6% of approved applicants, and this was the most influential factor pushing the decision toward bad credit. The second most influential factor was the 12-month requested duration. That is shorter than the approved average of about 19.17 months, and it actually worked in your favor by reducing the perceived risk. However, the third factor, your property status being unknown or none, also pushed toward bad credit; only about 7.8% of approved applicants had no known property, so the lack of recorded assets outweighed the benefit of the shorter term.
